searches.result: success; exact-concept search executed, but independent frequency/rank/company evidence was insufficient; prompts are original production adaptations and technical decisions use checked primary sources

sources.title: System Design Primer: Security
sources.supportRationale: Core conceptual orientation checked during specification; its brief section explicitly needs updates and is not the sole protocol/crypto authority or evidence of interview frequency.

sources.title: IETF RFC 9700: OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice
sources.supportRationale: Modern OAuth threat model, redirects, PKCE, client-specific refresh-token replay protection and scoped revocation concerns.

sources.title: IETF RFC 6749: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework
sources.supportRationale: OAuth roles, authorization-code exchange and access/refresh token responsibilities, read with current security BCPs rather than obsolete defaults.

sources.title: IETF RFC 10017: OAuth 2.0 for Browser-Based Applications
sources.supportRationale: Browser OAuth threats and architectural boundaries including BFFs, checked as the published August 2026 BCP rather than an old draft.

sources.title: IETF RFC 8725: JSON Web Token Best Current Practices
sources.supportRationale: Algorithm verification, trusted keys, issuer/audience and distinct JWT usage profiles; not a universal authorization or revocation protocol.

scenarios.theme: Two tabs refresh R0 at once and the session breaks. What changes?
scenarios.assumptions: The provider rotates and detects reuse, while the browser has no refresh coordination. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Refresh Token Rotation to two tabs.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Two tabs refresh R0 at once and the session breaks. What changes?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Coalesce refresh attempts within the supported client architecture and share the resulting session state safely, while retaining server-side atomic transit

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Cross-tab coordination adds complexity and does not stop a thief

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Disabling replay checks globally trades away the intended protection rather than fixing client reliability.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to bcp, browser; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A browser app embeds a client secret to protect refresh. Is that sufficient?

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Use the correct public-client security model with supported replay protection, or move confidential-client responsibilities to an appropriate backend/BFF w
